r0020: 6.  On 4 April 2000 the Court decided to give notice to the respondent Government of the complaints under Article 6 § 1 of the Convention and declared the remainder of the application inadmissible.
r0021: 7.  Both the applicant and the Government filed written observations on the admissibility and merits of the case.
r0022: 8.  On 1 November 2001 the Court changed the composition of its Sections (Rule 25 § 1). This case was assigned to the newly composed Third Section (Rule 52 § 1).
r0023: 9.  By a letter of 7 May 2002, the Court informed the parties that, in accordance with Article 29 §§ 1 and 3 of the Convention, it would rule on both the admissibility and the merits of the application. It also invited the parties to submit their additional observations on the merits of the case, and the applicant to submit his claims for just satisfaction.
r0024: 10.  On 10 June 2002 the applicant submitted to the Court his additional observations on the merits of the case together with his claim for just satisfaction.
r0025: 11.  By a letter of 19 June 2002, the Government submitted their comments on the claim for just satisfaction.
r0027: I.  THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE
r0028: 12.  The applicant, Yaşar Özel, is a Turkish national who was born in 1961 and is currently detained in Bayrampaşa Prison in Istanbul.
r0029: 13.  On 13 October 1994 the applicant and a certain C.A. were arrested by police officers from the public order branch of the Gayrettepe (İstanbul) Security Directorate. They were suspected of having committed a burglary at a jeweller’s shop. The applicant was placed in police custody for eight days on the premises of that branch. He was then transferred to the anti-terrorism branch of the same directorate, where he remained for seven days.
